title: FLUX.1
hook: FLUX.1 became the leading open-weight image model — from the Black Forest Labs team that built Stable Diffusion, now shipping a frontier-quality model you can run yourself.
key_points: Text-to-image model from Black Forest Labs, founded by former Stable Diffusion authors (2024).
FLUX.1 [schnell] is Apache 2.0; [dev] is open-weight under a non-commercial license.
Set a high bar for open-weight image quality and prompt-following.
[schnell] uses adversarial distillation to generate images in just 1–4 steps.
content_html: FLUX.1 is a family of text-to-image models from Black Forest Labs, the German lab founded in 2024 by Robin Rombach, Andreas Blattmann, and Patrick Esser — the researchers behind Stable Diffusion. Released open-weight, FLUX.1 quickly became the strongest openly available image model, combining high visual quality with notably better prompt-following than earlier open diffusion models.
extra_html:
What's new

The release came in tiers: FLUX.1 [schnell] under the permissive Apache 2.0 license, FLUX.1 [dev] as open weights under a non-commercial license, and a hosted [pro] tier. [schnell] is trained with latent adversarial diffusion distillation so it can generate high-quality images in just one to four sampling steps, making it fast and cheap to run locally. The lab later added control tools and editing-focused variants like FLUX.1 Kontext.

Why it matters

With Stability AI's momentum fading, FLUX.1 inherited the open-image crown and kept a competitive open ecosystem alive against closed leaders like Midjourney and the big labs' image models. For builders, an Apache-licensed model that runs in a few steps on consumer hardware is the foundation countless image apps and fine-tunes are built on.

related.title: SDXL: Improving Latent Diffusion for High-Resolution Synthesis
related.hook: A larger UNet, two text encoders, and a refinement diffusion stage gave open-source Stable Diffusion a major quality leap - now the workhorse of community image generation.

related.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion (Stable Diffusion)
related.hook: Running diffusion on raw pixels is brutally expensive. Do it in a compressed latent space instead, and high-res text-to-image becomes cheap enough to run on a consumer GPU.

related.title: Imagen: Photorealistic Text-to-Image Diffusion
related.hook: Google found that a large frozen T5 text encoder matters more than a bigger image diffusion model - scaling language understanding is the key lever for photorealistic generation.

related.title: Moebius: 0.2B Inpainting Rivaling 10B
related.hook: A 0.22B image-inpainting model that matches an 11.9B generalist (FLUX.1-Fill-Dev) — under 2% of the parameters and 15x faster — by pairing a linear-interaction backbone with latent-space distillation.

related.title: Nunchaku: 4-bit Diffusion Inference in Diffusers
related.hook: Diffusion models hate 4-bit — activation outliers wreck image quality. SVDQuant peels the hardest weights into a tiny 16-bit low-rank branch, and Nunchaku now runs it inside Diffusers.
